tech.name: Suction & ground sealing
tech.summary: A fan car can create downforce without waiting for high road speed.
tech.how: Tesla describes powered fans that remove air from beneath the car, together with ground sealing. The resulting pressure difference can press the vehicle toward the surface. Unlike a wing, the basic mechanism does not need forward airflow.
tech.why: More normal load can increase the tyre forces available for acceleration, braking and cornering. Surface sealing, fan power, debris, ride height and control behaviour all affect what a real system can deliver.
tech.boundary: Tesla says the system can hold the vehicle upside down at rest. The reveal is a controlled demonstration, not a published downforce map or an independent road-car test. Fan power, suction levels and the full operating envelope are not published here.

tech.name: Active aerodynamics
tech.summary: Road, low-drag and high-downforce settings address different jobs.
tech.how: Tesla describes deployable aero and a Track Mode that lowers the car and changes the suspension. Wing position and airflow management can trade drag against downforce as conditions change.
tech.why: Reducing drag supports efficiency and high-speed running. Adding downforce can help tyres generate larger cornering and braking forces, with an energy and drag trade-off.
tech.boundary: These diagrams explain the principles. They are not a measured aerodynamic model, a wind-tunnel result or a guaranteed mode availability list for every configuration.

tech.name: Cold-gas thrust
tech.summary: Stored gas expelled through nozzles produces a reaction force.
tech.how: A cold-gas thruster uses stored pressure rather than combustion to expel gas. Rear-facing outlets can add forward force; other orientations can support vertical and rotational control. Tesla describes electrically actuated control and frequent adjustments.
tech.why: This introduces forces that are not transmitted through the tyre contact patches. It also introduces a finite propellant supply, pressure-vessel mass, refill demands and a new control problem.
tech.boundary: Thrust magnitude, usable duration, pressure limits and refill time are not established by these images. Rocket is described as invite only and not approved for public road use; availability is regional.

tech.name: Pressure storage
tech.summary: A composite pressure vessel is a structural system, not a battery specification.
tech.how: Composite-overwrapped pressure vessels use an overwrap around a liner to contain high-pressure gas. The relevant design questions include usable gas mass, pressure, temperature, fatigue and how the vessels are supported and protected.
tech.why: More stored gas can extend a thruster system’s operating time, but packaging, vehicle mass and repeated-cycle performance matter. A published tank volume alone cannot determine flight time.
tech.boundary: No tank pressure, certified life, refill time or system energy budget is verified here. A pressure-vessel layout is not a substitute for production safety documentation.

tech.name: Steer-by-wire & cockpit
tech.summary: The physical controls and information layout are designed as one system.
tech.how: Tesla describes a yoke designed for steer-by-wire, a central touchscreen and two smaller forward displays. Its current page also describes manual controls and a fixed seat position as part of its mass-reduction approach.
tech.why: Steer-by-wire separates steering input sensing from a conventional mechanical linkage. Feedback, redundancy, calibration and the placement of information become central engineering questions.
tech.boundary: A cockpit image cannot verify steering feel, redundancy architecture, adjustable control ranges or the final production equipment list.

tech.name: Mass & materials
tech.summary: Materials, packaging and control choices affect the entire vehicle.
tech.how: Tesla lists magnesium, titanium and carbon fibre among the materials used throughout the vehicle. Its published imagery shows the mechanical package; the exact contribution of each material is not quantified.
tech.why: Lower mass can reduce the force and energy needed for a given manoeuvre. Stiffness, crash performance, durability, manufacturing and cost still need to be balanced.
tech.boundary: Production curb weight, battery capacity, charging performance and a validated range test are not established by this material list. The old 2017 battery and range promises are not treated as current specifications.

configs.name: Performance
features: Two seats · fan suction & active aero
configs.note: Reported equipment is subject to change. “Road ready” is Tesla’s positioning; final certification depends on market.
equipment: Dihedral doors with removable roof panels
Active Track Mode; active wings and barge boards; hidden aero
Powered fan-and-skirt system with multi-mode suction and ground sealing
Individually controlled brake-corner actuation; carbon-ceramic brakes
Spool-valve adaptive dampers; reported track stiffness more than triples and ride height drops up to 40 mm
Fixed seat base with adjustable recline; adjustable pedal bay; selected manual controls
exclusions: No thrusters, COPVs or rocket-assisted acceleration
No gold-tinted glass or Supersonic interior package
reportedSpecs: Over 300 miles; described as EPA range in the report, not a certified result here

configs.name: Thrust
features: One pressure vessel · four rear thrusters
configs.note: October target: under 0.9 seconds; Tesla’s product-page wording is under one second. Neither is an independently verified production-car result.
equipment: Performance equipment, plus one carbon-overwrapped pressure vessel (COPV)
Four rear thrusters for acceleration; electric Optimus actuators
Supersonic interior: Ultrawhite surfaces, grey microsuede detailing and seat bolsters, plus a yoke with two smaller forward displays
exclusions: No second COPV, downward lift-control thrusters or side yaw-control thrusters
reportedSpecs: Over 300 miles; described as EPA range in the report, not a certified result here

configs.name: Rocket
configs.note: Reported equipment is subject to change. Tesla says Rocket is not approved for public road use; availability is regional.
equipment: Applicable Performance and Thrust features, with a single-seat layout
Two COPVs; ten total thrusters: four rear for acceleration, four downward perimeter for lift control and two side for yaw control
All-electric Optimus actuators; gold-tinted glass; Supersonic interior
Ano White exterior paint with reported UV and cryogenic protection, electrostatic dissipation and corrosion resistance
reportedSpecs: Over 300 miles; described as EPA range in the report, not a certified result here
